text:
emily_support: FYI customer reported a spike of '5xx' billing events during streaming. They see abrupt 'broken pipe' in client logs but our gateway marked it 502 and billed tokens. customer says tokens billed despite client closing early. 
ryan_eng: @emily_support can you drop the trace_id and sample request headers? suspecting TLS half-close from proxy pool.
maria_support: Added traceback from customer: 
```
client: EOFError: connection reset by peer
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection was reset
headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked; Connection: keep-alive; User-Agent: acme-client/2.1
```
emily_support: Trace: trace=tr_9a8b7c, sample request body small chat stream (few tokens), they use our hosted endpoint via corporate proxy. Reported repro with VSCode extension.
ryan_eng: looking at traces for tr_9a8b7c — I see our gateway returned 502 because upstream proxy sent FIN before last chunk trailer. Gateway's stream classifier currently marks that as gateway error and counts as 5xx. We should differentiate client-initiated half-close vs upstream error.
ops_oncall: @ryan_eng any quick mitigation? customer is asking for credit and unbilled tokens.
ryan_eng: short-term: add a heuristic to look for TCP FIN from client IP vs gateway origin. If FIN from client-side and we already sent final token frames, treat as client close (do not bill). Will push a rule to edge flags.
proxybot: deploybot: flag/edge-rule 0.3.11 scheduled to rollout to 25% in 10m windows.
maria_support: Customer asks for repro steps — I tried to reproduce locally but need the proxy behavior. Do we have a curl recipe to simulate TLS half-close?
ryan_eng: yes — try this sequence: open a raw TLS connection, send request with chunked body, then immediate FIN before trailer. Quick curl variant: 
```
# open conn and send chunk without trailer, then close socket
printf 'POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.com\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n5\nhello\n' | openssl s_client -quiet -connect api.redwood.com:443
# then close the socket from client side (ctrl-c) to simulate half-close
```
ryan_eng: On our side, we saw pattern: upstream FIN arrives BEFORE gateway writes final 0\r\n\r\n so gateway assumes truncation and classifies as 502. We should treat absence of trailer + upstream FIN within 200ms of last data as client abort, not server error.
emily_support: Customer provided sample payload and timestamp. Asking for timeline for rollback or credit.
ops_oncall: I'll escalate to billing: recommend provisional credit while eng ships edge rule. Need comms phrasing.
maria_support: Drafting message: "we identified a proxy TLS half-close causing premature FINs which our gateway misclassified as a server error. We're deploying a classifier fix and will credit affected tokens; ETA ~3 hours for canary, 24 hours full rollout." Thoughts?
ryan_eng: good. Also log a follow-up to improve chunked parsing: if trailing chunk '0\r\n' missing but socket from client IP closed, treat as client disconnect. Also add metric for 'proxy halfclose' to catch regression.
emily_support: customer wants repro steps in case they want to reproduce — I'll include the curl/openssl snippet and note it's reproducible with corporate proxies that aggressively tear connections.
ops_oncall: rolling the edge-rule now. proxybot: deploy started: canary->25% -> 10m -> monitor 5xx rate.
ryan_eng: monitoring: if 5xx streaming events drop and client-abort events increase, that means classifier flip worked. I'll follow in Sentry dashboards.
emily_support: sending interim reply to customer now. Will update thread when billing confirms credits. :thumbsup:
